gap: No result ChatGPT got states that adapter-plus-converter combos with a separate 2000 W hair-dryer outlet sell at the makers' own stores for $45.99–$49.99 (TESSAN 4-USB $45.99, BESTEK MRJ2001BU $46.99, Ceptics LX-C2000 $49.99), about what the 200–250 W units cost, or that those outlets exclude Dyson/Shark FlexStyle and other digitally controlled dryers, or that on the Ceptics LX2-M2000 and BESTEK's EU-plug 2000 W unit the 200 W outlet does not convert voltage at all.
standout_why: I compared against GlobalPlugs (voltage-converter-vs-adapter) and the VoltWander FAQ, and against ChatGPT's own answer with its two cards. GlobalPlugs names no products and says combined units are rated 'roughly 25-100 W' and should be avoided. TESSAN TC03 (250 W) and BESTEK (250/300 W) contradict that. VoltWander names no products and does not cover combo units. ChatGPT showed only 200–250 W units and said compact converters often can't handle hair dryers. None of these sources prices a combo with a 2000 W heating outlet, mentions the Dyson/digital-dryer exclusion, or warns that one outlet on some combos passes 220 V straight through. I could not read the TravelPowerPro guide (certificate error), the Digital Camera World Ceptics review (content truncated), or the TESSAN manuals.plus PDFs (compressed text), so they are not compared.
decides: The pick splits by device. For phones, laptops and small single-voltage electronics, the TESSAN TC03 ($43.99, 250 W, 2 USB-C + 2 USB-A, plugs C/G/I-A/F) holds as our pick. A US hair dryer is the most common reason shoppers ask this, and for it the answer changes from 'no compact combo does it' to 'a $46–50 combo with a 2000 W outlet does, if the dryer has mechanical switches.' Dyson and other digital dryers are excluded, and the shopper should use only the outlet that is labeled as converting.
